html:
SMTO-UI-0033 — An older saved queue couldn't be used

GUID: 18a8e7cc-fa4f-498d-beaa-9054d5f2e42d
Slug: ui-queue-snapshot-invalid
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO found an old saved copy of your message queue that it couldn't read. It can't tell whether those messages were already sent, so it didn't send them again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether the earlier action already happened: open the conversation and look at its recent messages and the Queued list above the message box. SMTO couldn't confirm which queued messages were already accepted, and some may have run.
  2. Reload the page so it shows the queue SMTO is keeping now. The current queue is kept by SMTO itself, so a fresh page shows what is really waiting.
  3. Only send a message again if it is missing from both the conversation and the Queued list. Sending a message that was already accepted would make SMTO do the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • Every message you meant to send appears exactly once, in the conversation or the Queued list.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend all your old messages at once; any that already ran would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A retained diagnostic reports an invalid historical browser queue snapshot; current builds have no direct emitter for this alias because the queue is now a server-owned conversation task lane.

What this means

  • This historical alias refers to an invalid browser queue snapshot; the current UI projects an authoritative server-owned conversation lane. No direct current emitter for this retained alias was found. Inspect the original occurrence and current control state before assuming a particular validation ran or a submission was prevented.

Why this can happen

  • This historical alias refers to an invalid browser queue snapshot; the current UI projects an authoritative server-owned conversation lane.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the original snapshot version and reconcile its submission identities with the server lane.

How to fix it

  • This is a retained alias (ui_queue_snapshot_invalid) with no current browser emitter; the task lane at the conversation's task-lane endpoint (GET /api/agent/conversations/:conversation_id/task-lane) is authoritative. Keep the original occurrence, compare its submission IDs with the tasks currently in the lane, and only resubmit prompts that have no accepted task.
  • Preserve the old snapshot and reconcile exact submission identities against the current server-owned lane.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Pending items are recovered without duplicating already accepted tasks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • No direct current emitter for this retained alias was found. Inspect the original occurrence and current control state before assuming a particular validation ran or a submission was prevented.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
